She describes the pain as a sharp, burning sensation that worsens with neck movement.
She also reports numbness in her left thumb and index finger.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset abdominal pain and lip swelling consistent with known hereditary angioedema

lines: Sudden-onset abdominal pain and lip swelling consistent with known hereditary angioedema
The patient, known to have hereditary angioedema with C1 inhibitor deficiency and status post open cholecystectomy, presents to the Emergency Department with acute abdominal pain.
The abdominal pain began 4 hours ago and is described as deep, crampy, and non-radiating.
Her parents report that she has had multiple similar episodes since early childhood, occasionally accompanied by swelling of her face, extremities, or genitalia.
These episodes typically last 2–3 days and resolve spontaneously.
She was previously treated with antihistamines, but they have never been effective.
She denies rash, fever, or any recent illness.
- Cervical radiculopathy due to C6-C7 intervertebral disc herniation (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Cervical degenerative disc disease with C6-C7 herniation
No known drug allergies, No known food allergies
Her maternal uncle reportedly died from unexplained throat swelling in his 20s.
Her blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg, pulse is 105/min, and respirations are 28/min.
On physical exam, she is afebrile but appears uncomfortable.
She has perioral swelling without urticaria and diffuse abdominal tenderness to palpation, but no rebound or guarding.
Bowel sounds are hyperactive, and no organomegaly is present.
A CT scan of the abdomen shows bowel wall edema and small-volume ascites.

encounters.cc: Intermittent severe headaches, palpitations, and diaphoresis occurring over the past few months

lines: Intermittent severe headaches, palpitations, and diaphoresis occurring over the past few months

This 47-year-old female with hypertension, hereditary angioedema, cervical disc disease, and prior evaluation for cervical radiculopathy and acoustic neuroma reports severe headaches, palpitations, and diaphoresis.
These symptoms have been occurring intermittently over the past few months but have become more frequent and intense.
She denies any chest pain, dyspnea, or recent illness.
- Cervical radiculopathy due to C6-C7 intervertebral disc herniation (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Cervical degenerative disc disease with C6-C7 herniation
No known drug allergies, No known food allergies
Her family history is significant for her father who had thyroid cancer.
Her blood pressure is 220/110 mmHg, heart rate is 118 bpm, and she is afebrile.
Physical examination reveals a well-nourished woman in distress due to a headache.
Her skin is notably moist, and she has a fine tremor.
An ECG shows sinus tachycardia with no ST or T wave changes.
The patient is given intravenous phentolamine, after which her blood pressure decreases to 150/90 mmHg and her symptoms improve.

lines: Acute onset palpitations and lightheadedness while gardening 30 minutes ago

She presents with palpitations and lightheadedness that started while she was gardening 30 minutes ago.
- Cervical radiculopathy due to C6-C7 intervertebral disc herniation (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Cervical degenerative disc disease with C6-C7 herniation
She has a history of hypertension, well-controlled on hydrochlorothiazide, and no known cardiac disease.
No known drug allergies, No known food allergies
- Mother: Hereditary angioedema (confirmed C1 inhibitor deficiency)
- Father: Hypertension, cerebrovascular accident at age 60
On examination, her blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 170 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Her lungs are clear to auscultation, and there is no leg swelling.
The cardiac monitor shows a narrow-QRS-complex tachycardia without visible P waves.
An intravenous line is established, and adenosine is administered.
Shortly after administration, the heart rate slows, and distinct P waves with a sawtooth pattern are observed before the tachycardia resumes.

encounters.cc: Sudden dizziness, vomiting, and difficulty walking after neck extension while painting ceiling

lines: Sudden dizziness, vomiting, and difficulty walking after neck extension while painting ceiling

The patient is a 49-year-old female with known cervical degenerative disc disease and C6-C7 herniation previously evaluated for radiculopathy who presents with symptoms that started 2 hours ago after she extended her neck to paint her ceiling.
She reports that the room seems to be spinning around her, and she has vomited twice.
She also notes numbness on the left side of her face and weakness in her right arm and leg.
- Cervical radiculopathy due to C6-C7 intervertebral disc herniation (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

On examination, her blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, heart rate is 85 beats per minute, and she is afebrile.
Neurological examination reveals decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick on the left side of her face and decreased strength in the right upper and lower extremities.
The remainder of the cranial nerve examination is normal.
Head CT without contrast shows no acute abnormalities.
